title: Governor 2025: A Contest in Full Gear - Insider NJ
content: The article reports on the 2025 New Jersey governor race between Republican Jack Ciattarelli and Democrat Mikie Sherrill, describing the campaign as a high‑stakes, over‑the‑top contest.  It notes that both parties are pushing hard, with Ciattarelli attempting to distance himself from Trump while Sherrill seeks to broaden her appeal beyond her suburban base.  A Republican insider is quoted as saying, 'We're going to win,' and later, 'Game over,' highlighting the GOP’s confidence.  Sherrill’s background is highlighted: she is a former Navy helicopter pilot and a congresswoman who flipped a suburban red district, and she has received an endorsement from Newark Mayor Ras Baraka.  The article cites registration data, stating that the state Secretary of State’s Office shows 860,000 more registered Democrats than Republicans, but also that Republican registrations have jumped by about 35% compared to a 20% increase for Democrats.  It discusses campaign themes such as the affordability crisis, property‑tax concerns, and the influence of Trump, noting that Sherrill must avoid over‑relying on Trump while Ciattarelli seeks to shed his ‘albatross’.  Overall, the piece frames the race as a volatile, emotionally charged showdown with both sides portrayed in dramatic, sensational language.

title: Democrat Mikie Sherrill holds cash lead in NJ governor's race • New Jersey Monitor
content: In the 2025 New Jersey gubernatorial race, Democrat Mikie Sherrill holds a financial lead over Republican Jack Ciattarelli. Since June, Sherrill raised $17.5 million, surpassing Ciattarelli’s $16.5 million. As of October 3, Sherrill had $6.5 million in campaign reserves, compared to Ciattarelli’s nearly $4 million. Ciattarelli spent $12.6 million in the race, slightly more than Sherrill’s $11 million. Both candidates received public matching funds under New Jersey’s public financing program, which matches donations at a 2-to-1 ratio up to $12.5 million in matching funds and requires spending limits of $18.5 million. Sherrill received $10.5 million in matching funds, including $801,619 not reflected in her latest filing, while Ciattarelli received $9.6 million. The majority of both campaigns’ spending went to media: Ciattarelli spent $11 million on media, including $4.8 million on network TV ads and $3.6 million on digital ads, significantly outpacing Sherrill’s $970,645 in digital ads. Sherrill spent $2.8 million on cable ads, more than double Ciattarelli’s $964,494. Sherrill’s $4.2 million in mixed media spending likely included television and digital ads, according to Micah Rasmussen of Rider University’s Rebovich Institute. Radio ads were a minor expense: Ciattarelli spent $121,772, including a $1,000 ad on New Jersey 101.5, while Sherrill spent $314,058. Newspaper ads were minimal: Sherrill spent $14,050 on Spanish-language and Jewish newspapers, and Ciattarelli made one ad buy in the Italian Tribune. Sherrill, a four-term congresswoman and member of the majority party, benefits from prior fundraising experience and party advantage, while Ciattarelli, a former GOP nominee, has improved his fundraising pace from his 2021 campaign, when he raised $10.1 million 29 days before Election Day.

title: Rutgers-Eagleton: Sherrill Leads by Nine Points Among Likely Voters in 2025 Race for New Jersey Governor - Insider NJ
content: The latest Rutgers‑Eagleton Poll shows Democratic nominee Mikie Sherrill leading Republican candidate Jack Ciattarelli by nine percentage points among likely voters in New Jersey’s 2025 gubernatorial race. Forty‑four percent of respondents say they would vote for Sherrill if the election were held today, versus 35 percent for Ciattarelli, with 3 percent for neither or someone else and 17 percent undecided. When leaners are added, 47 percent back Sherrill and 37 percent back Ciattarelli.  The poll notes that 85 percent of Democrats would vote for Sherrill and 81 percent of Republicans for Ciattarelli, while independents are almost evenly split (33 percent for Sherrill, 32 percent for Ciattarelli, 29 percent undecided).  Demographic breakdowns show Sherrill’s strongest support among Black voters (69 percent to 4 percent), Hispanic voters (56 percent to 22 percent), and Asian voters (47 percent to 18 percent).  Women are 11 points less likely than men to back Ciattarelli and nine points more likely to be undecided.  Sherrill leads 48 percent to 21 percent among 18‑34 year olds, but her advantage narrows to 47 percent to 29 percent among 35‑49 year olds and 48 percent to 38 percent among 65‑plus voters, disappearing among 50‑64 year olds (36 percent to 41 percent).  Socioeconomic data show Sherrill performs best with voters holding at least a college degree (53 percent to 26 percent) and with households earning $150,000 or more annually (58 percent to 28 percent).  Geographically, Sherrill’s largest margins come from urban (46 percent to 23 percent) and suburban (49 percent to 30 percent) voters; exurban, southern, and shore regions are nearly split.  Pollster Ashley Koning remarked, 'We are also at a turning point in New Jersey politics…the only thing for certain is that all eyes are on New Jersey this cycle.'

title: Put A Woman in Charge. Mikie Sherrill For Governor. - Insider NJ
content: The article 'Put A Woman in Charge. Mikie Sherrill For Governor.' by Insider NJ argues for the election of Democratic U.S. Congresswoman Mikie Sherrill as New Jersey's next governor, emphasizing her qualifications and leadership potential amid a contentious gubernatorial race against Republican nominee Jack Ciattarelli. Sherrill, who emerged victorious in a competitive Democratic primary, is portrayed as a trailblazing female leader with a proven record of achievement, including a 'bio-centric primary campaign' that highlighted her credentials as one of the most impressive in the U.S. Congress. The article notes that her campaign faced a significant setback when an unredacted version of her military record—containing her Social Security number and personal data—was leaked by a branch of the National Archives, described as a 'politically motivated disclosure.' Sherrill’s team successfully reframed the incident as a smear tactic, turning it into an opportunity to expose the attack and reaffirm their integrity. The article criticizes the Ciattarelli campaign for undermining the race with unfounded accusations and a lack of civility, which it claims has diminished the quality of debate and left voters without meaningful insights into either candidate’s governance plans. Sherrill’s focus on affordability, federal infrastructure funding, and support for families is presented as a compelling alternative. The piece underscores the historical context: New Jersey has not seen three consecutive terms for either party since 1961, and the sitting president’s party typically does not benefit in gubernatorial elections here. Despite these challenges, the article concludes that Sherrill’s resilience and track record make her uniquely positioned to lead, calling for a historic moment by 'putting Mikie Sherrill in charge.'

title: Elecciones 2025: quiénes son los candidatos a gobernador en Nueva Jersey
content: The 2025 New Jersey general election is scheduled for November 4, 2025, with voting hours from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. The gubernatorial race features four candidates: Mikie Sherrill (Democrat), Jack Ciattarelli (Republican), Vic Kaplan (Libertarian), and Joanne Kuniansky (Socialist Workers Party). Sherrill, a former Navy officer and current U.S. Congresswoman for New Jersey's 11th district, holds a doctorate in law from Georgetown University and a master’s from the London School of Economics. Ciattarelli, a Republican with prior experience in the New Jersey General Assembly and county government, is endorsed by former President Donald Trump. Kaplan represents the Libertarian Party, advocating for limited government and individual freedoms. Kuniansky, from the Socialist Workers Party, focuses on labor rights, social justice, and workers' defense. The vice gubernatorial race includes Dale Caldwell (Democrat), James Gannon (Republican), Bruno Pereira (Libertarian), and Craig Honts (Socialist Workers Party), each aligned with their respective gubernatorial candidates. Voter registration closes on October 14, 2025, with absentee ballots available until October 28 (by mail) or October 3 (in person). Early voting runs from October 25 to November 2, 2025. Additionally, the election will renew all 80 seats in the New Jersey General Assembly, where Democrats currently hold 52 seats and Republicans 28. Local elections, including school board races in Newark (April) and Jersey City (November 4), and a special election in Legislative District 35 to fill a vacancy, will also take place. The outcome of the legislative majority will significantly influence the new governor’s ability to implement policies.

title: The New Jersey governor’s race is here. America is watching. - New Jersey Globe
content: New Jersey’s gubernatorial race between Democrat Rep. Mikie Sherrill and Republican former Assemblyman Jack Ciattarelli has become a national focal point. Analysts say the contest will serve as a bellwether for 2026 midterms. National groups are pouring money: the Democratic Governors Association announced a $20 million spend on ads for Sherrill, up from $2.3 million in 2021, while the Republican Governors Association has not disclosed a figure but historically spent $3.8 million in 2021. Sherrill’s campaign ties the race to President Trump, citing his endorsement and policy positions, whereas Ciattarelli has highlighted local issues but also leveraged his Trump backing. Quotes: Matthew Klein of the Cook Political Report said, 'New Jersey and Virginia are the first real tests of where things stand, and they’re important trial balloons for messaging ahead of 2024.' Mo Butler, a Democratic strategist, added, 'People figuratively say, ‘The eyes of the nation will be on us,’' and Janice Fields said, 'They want to help in any way they can – ‘we want to take a bus to New Jersey and help you…’' The article notes that a Sherrill victory would give Democrats momentum for 2026, while a Ciattarelli win would signal Republican resilience. It also discusses how the governor will influence the appointment of the state attorney general and the state Supreme Court, with implications for national policy debates.

title: Sherrill dinged by new GOP House challenger over missed votes - New Jersey Globe
content: Rep. Mikie Sherrill (D-Montclair) has faced criticism from her Republican challenger, Joe Hathaway, in New Jersey’s 11th congressional district over her absence from numerous House votes due to her campaign for governor. Hathaway, the Randolph mayor, argued that skipping half of her duties would make him accountable as mayor and called on Sherrill to return half of her congressional salary, stating, 'If Mikie truly believes members of Congress shouldn’t get paid when they aren’t doing their jobs, then she should return half of her taxpayer-funded salary immediately.' Sherrill’s spokesperson, Sean Higgins, defended her actions, emphasizing that she is actively fighting against Trump and Republican healthcare cuts and the Gateway Tunnel attack, which are critical to New Jersey residents. Higgins also criticized Hathaway, saying he lacks the backbone to stand up to threats to the state. Sherrill acknowledged in 2024 that she would not be present for every vote but committed to working with Democratic leaders to be present when needed. Hathaway’s campaign serves as a political tool for Governor Jack Ciattarelli and the New Jersey GOP, framing Sherrill as neglectful of her constituents by focusing on her gubernatorial ambitions. Hathaway stated, 'New Jersey families deserve a representative who shows up for them,' accusing Sherrill of prioritizing political ambition over her congressional duties.
